entities.summary:
Publius Decius Mus, son of Quintus, of the plebeian gens Decia, was a Roman consul in 340 BC. He is noted particularly for sacrificing himself in battle through the ritual of devotio, as recorded by the Augustan historian Livy.




This act of self-sacrifice was a pivotal moment in Roman history, cementing the Decian tradition of devotio in Roman warfare. The ritual, in which a soldier would be sacrificed to the gods in exchange for victory, became a hallmark of Roman military strategy.




Decius' decision to undergo devotio in battle had a profound impact on the Roman Republic, influencing the development of Roman military tactics and the cult of the Roman state.




Despite the significance of his sacrifice, Publius Decius Mus remains a lesser-known figure in Roman history, overshadowed by his more famous contemporaries.
